summary: A security deposit must not be more than one month's rent.
explanation: Under Irish law, a landlord cannot ask for a security deposit that is greater than one month's rent. This applies to all new tenancies created on or after August 9, 2021.
recommended_action: Inform the landlord that under the Residential Tenancies Act, a deposit cannot exceed one month's rent. State that you will be paying the legal amount of €[one month's rent]. If they refuse, you can report this to the Residential Tenancies Board (RTB).

summary: The landlord must acknowledge receipt of the deposit in writing.
explanation: Your landlord should provide you with a written receipt that states the amount of the deposit paid and the date it was paid. This is an important record for you to keep.
compliant_examples: Landlord will provide written receipt within 21 days
Receipt will be issued upon payment
recommended_action: Ensure you receive a written receipt for your deposit payment. If not provided, request one in writing from your landlord. Keep this receipt safe as proof of payment.

summary: Deposits must be returned within 10 days of the tenancy ending, unless there are valid deductions.
explanation: Your landlord must return your deposit within 10 days of the tenancy ending, unless they have valid reasons for deductions (damage beyond normal wear and tear, unpaid rent, etc.).
compliant_examples: Deposit will be returned within 10 days
Refund within 10 days of tenancy end
Return within 10 days unless deductions apply
recommended_action: Ensure the lease specifies a 10-day return timeline. If not, discuss this with your landlord and request the clause be amended. If they refuse, you can enforce this through the RTB.
